title: Maximum Binary String After Change
statement:
`binary` is a string made of the characters `'0'` and `'1'`. You may apply the following two moves as many times as you like (including zero times), in any order:

- pick any occurrence of `"00"` and turn it into `"10"`;
- pick any occurrence of `"10"` and turn it into `"01"`.

The moves never change the length. Return the largest string you can end up with, where one string is larger than another when the binary number it spells has a greater value.
notes:
## Intuition

Exploring every reachable string works only for tiny inputs. Think about what the moves can do instead. The ones before the first `'0'` are already as good as possible, so leave them alone. After that point, `"10" → "01"` lets a zero hop left over a one, so every zero can be slid left until all zeros form one block starting at the first zero. Then `"00" → "10"` turns a block of `z` zeros into `z - 1` ones followed by a single `'0'`. One zero always survives: `"00"` is the only move that removes a zero, and it needs two of them. So the best string is all ones except one `'0'` at index `firstZero + zeros - 1`.

## Approach

1. Find `firstZero`. If there is none, the string is all ones and already maximal; return it.
2. Count the zeros from `firstZero` to the end in `zeros`.
3. The surviving zero sits at `zeroAt = firstZero + zeros - 1`.
4. Build a string of ones of the same length and put a `'0'` at `zeroAt`.

## Example 1, step by step

`binary = "000110"`. `firstZero = 0`. Zeros occur at indices 0, 1, 2 and 5, so `zeros = 4` and `zeroAt = 0 + 4 - 1 = 3`. Six ones with a zero at index 3 give `"111011"`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one scan to find and count zeros, one to build the answer.
- Space: O(n) for the returned string.

## Pitfalls

- An all-ones string must be returned unchanged; without the early return, `zeroAt` would be `-2` and the answer would be wrong.
- Applying the moves directly on the string is slow (each move is O(n) and there can be O(n²) of them) and greedy replacement can stall early; compute the final shape instead.
- The answer always keeps exactly one zero when the input has any: `"10"` stays `"10"`, it cannot become `"11"`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `firstZero` | index of the first `'0'`, or `-1` if none |
| `zeros` | number of zeros at or after `firstZero` |
| `i` | scanning index while counting |
| `zeroAt` | index of the one zero left in the answer |
| `ones` | string of `'1'` with the input's length |

narration.2: Ones in front of the first zero can never improve, so find where the zeros begin.
narration.3: No zero at all means every digit is already 1.
narration.4: Nothing can be improved; return the string as it is.
narration.7: Walk from the first zero to the end of the string.
narration.8: Each zero found here joins the block that forms at firstZero.
narration.12: A block of zeros collapses to ones with a single zero at its last position.
narration.13: Start from a string of all ones of the same length.
narration.14: Place the one surviving zero at zeroAt and return the result.
